parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, document rule, facility ban, police targeting, or violence record appears; visitor accounts describe a relaxed reception. Against that: a subdued climate of homophobia with no LGBT infrastructure, no non-discrimination protection covering gender identity (a resident gap, though it leaves an outed visitor without recourse), religious hostility to imposed decriminalisation, and a real conditional exposure — an age-of-consent differential that classifies a trans visitor's relationship as same-sex conduct, carrying prosecution risk a different-sex couple does not face. Dossier is thin on trans-specific matters (documents, facilities, custody, care all unresolved), so I extrapolate from the structural picture: no criminalisation of expression, but no documented acceptance of gender diversity and thin recourse. Sexuality-law factors are secondary here and decriminalised; they hold the score a step below acceptance-with-protections tiers.
